title: The grain fleet
terrain: three lashed decks; open water at every edge; no terrain to hide behind
design_note: VOYAGE not battle: the fleet is under way and the objective is landfall. Privateers board from the map edges. GRAPPLE LINES ARE THE DENS -- each is a capturable structure that stops producing when cut, so boarding is an objective, not an ambush. Fliers dominant, riding impossible, armor sinks if it goes over the side. The Assembly could not build this fleet, so it bought one; the privateers were paid for in Anbar.
approaches: the weather deck|below, through the hold|the rigging (flying only)

title: Ur-Nashet, the last night
terrain: hanging gardens in rain: stepped terraces (+1 cost when wet), irrigation channels, one aqueduct span
design_note: PROLOGUE. Breaks the map laws on purpose -- a flashback is a memory, and memories are unreliable in the direction of making you look stronger than you were. No permadeath, no dens, no requisition, no forge, one weapon each, no repair. The garrison is fatigued and not a threat. The living patron stands over the temple terrace, never moves, never attacks, has no health bar, and watches. It goes still only AFTER the image is rubble and the scribe writes -- you cannot write down a god that people can still see.
approaches: the terraces (foot)|the aqueduct span (one tile)|the channels (flying only)

title: His Lake
terrain: the hermit's lake: his island on the north shore, Pelagos (the fisher commune) on the south, open water between that only the Isles' own pilots cross safely -- except one known shallow ford
design_note: Regrounded (2026-09-23) once locations.loc_hermit_lake/polities.pol_isles/settlements.set_pelagos were found (see ch_p_indech's own note for the correction and full connection). objective_verb='defend' was already set but turn_limit was 0, which silently made the defend-win condition (map_grid.gd's _check_defend_win, limit>0 required) unreachable -- set to 8, matching map_a02/map_v22/map_m22's precedent for the same objective_verb. Terrain rebuilt around a real chokepoint: pol_isles.comparative_advantage ('pilotage -- the Isles' crews are why anyone crosses safely') implies the open water isn't safely crossable without a local pilot, so a raiding ea_warlord reaching Pelagos needs a ford -- that ford, not the lake itself, is what's actually being defended. ea_warlord's movement_type is infantry (enemy_archetypes), so it can use the foot-only ford exactly like the player's own ground units; the old placeholder terrain had no ford at all, which would have made either side unable to reach the other.
approaches: the shores (foot)|the ford, 3 tiles wide (foot only)|open water (flying only)
